task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of October 29, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: A fire at Meridia Pharma's primary U.S. propofol manufacturing plant in Clearfield, Indiana, on October 22, 2024, destroyed the facility's largest fill-and-finish line, triggering a national propofol shortage.
Propofol is the most commonly used general anesthetic in U.S. operating rooms; roughly 50 million procedures annually require it.
The destroyed line produced approximately 40% of Meridia's U.S. propofol supply; Meridia holds a 58% share of the U.S. propofol market.
The FDA placed propofol on its critical shortage list on October 25 and issued import facilitation orders for two international manufacturers, Pharmax Belgium and Adena Laboratorios of Spain.
Hospital procurement officers said propofol allocations from distributors had already been cut by 25 to 35% at institutions they represent.

Dr. Patricia Lam, anesthesiology chief at a regional hospital, said: "We have shifted some elective cases to alternative agents, but propofol's pharmacokinetics — particularly how quickly patients wake up — cannot be fully replicated by any single substitute."
Meridia CEO Dr. Carlos Estrada said the company is redirecting output from its secondary plant in Arizona and expects the Clearfield line to be rebuilt within 12 to 18 months.
Cause of the fire is under investigation by the Indiana State Fire Marshal's office; no injuries were reported.
The FDA said it is monitoring substitution rates to track whether alternative agents are being used safely in patient populations for whom they are less appropriate.
Hospital networks in the Southeast and Midwest reported the most severe allocation constraints because of their greater dependence on Meridia as a regional distributor.
The two alternative intravenous anesthetics most commonly used in place of propofol are etomidate and ketamine; both have different sedation depth profiles and side effect spectrums.
The FDA's import facilitation does not waive good manufacturing practice requirements; imported product still requires FDA inspection or documentation of equivalence.

Drug policy researchers have noted the Meridia shortage as a case study in single-source dependence risk; one company held a majority U.S. market share with a single primary domestic manufacturing site.
No elective surgery cancellations have been publicly confirmed as of the October 29 reporting date, but hospital administrators said decisions about case prioritization were being made daily.
The FDA said it expects imported product from Pharmax Belgium to begin arriving within three weeks.
Propofol has a relatively short shelf life of 24 months from manufacture; building strategic reserves is therefore more difficult than for solid oral medications.
The U.S. drug shortage database lists 47 active shortages of sterile injectable medications; propofol is the highest-volume item on the current list.
Meridia stock fell 18% in the week after the fire, then partially recovered when the import facilitation was announced.
Dr. Lam noted that training programs for anesthesia providers focus heavily on propofol protocols; switching agents mid-shortage requires rapid in-service retraining.
Congressional members from Indiana have asked the FDA to provide monthly shortage status reports.
